newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal plant to fly parts to beat Spanish strike.
newsitem.headline: Portugal plant to fly parts to beat Spanish strike.

text.p: Portugal's Ford-Volkswagen AutoEuropa car manufacturer has ordered special flights and train deliveries of supplies in order to avoid a Spanish truckers' strike, an AutoEuropa source said on Thursday.
"We are taking special steps including flights of supplies and train deliveries, but we will maintain normal production today and tomorrow," the source told Reuters.
Supplies are usually delivered by road to the plant, Portugal's biggest car manufacturer, 30 miles (50 km) south of Lisbon.
"We will review production next Monday, depending on events in Spain," said the source, who had no further details.
The AutoEuropa plant is normally shut over the weekend.
The eight-day-old Spanish truck drivers' strike to demand improved labour conditions has throttled roads in almost all of northern Spain, cut off supplies to many areas and forced factories to shut.
A French truckers' strike last November disrupted production at AutoEuropa, which produces 510 passenger vans per day.
During that stoppage, AutoEuropa flew in supplies including engines, transmissions and air conditioning components.
